reading:
Pocket Timeline found its own voice in tour round 2. Pocket Diary (t2-pocket-graft, 8.03) had the round's highest mean, was heat a's only design in all eight top fours, and took all 8 promise votes. It won on typesetting. Every dated row on Home, Plans, To do and Chat is set as a diary sets a day: node, then a big light figure with the mono month over the weekday, then the time, the entry and how far off. Type and usability gave it 8.5, and system called it 'the date standard for every lineage'. The judges also love the lineage's older gains: the NOW, NEXT and LATER spine with lit plates; the four-week pulse trace on the NEXT tube with the weekends shaded, which style called 'the best data-in-light figure'; To do as a due queue cut by a lit NOW line, with Someday below it; the Plans agenda that folds its quiet weeks, beside the month tube with a pulse per plan; today's figure '30' lit; the chat ending in a NOW-tabbed box; condensed Instrument Sans heads over Plex Sans and Plex Mono; and pointing at a plan to light its pulse ('light that answers').

What held it back is a short, repeated list, most-cited first:
1. The amber '6 worth a look' at Status's head, for six routine end_turn calls. Seven lenses faulted it as a false alarm that spends amber's one job.
2. The wide dead gap in Home's full-width LATER (Lately added) rows. All eight lenses named it.
3. To do printing the time twice ('19:56', then 'due tomorrow, 19:56'). Six lenses.
4. The key in every footer: fine print, a crutch, 'a smell'. Style, system and the skeptic; soul, interaction and usability would keep it on the pages whose marks need it.
5. The row afterglow is still invisible. Pocket's sage stepped edge never showed. Lessons say the edge must be phosphor green and visible at 120ms.
6. Tracked VT323 caps on the NOW, NEXT, LATER and Someday plates (type).
7. The To do checkbox sits on the spine, about 200px from its title, and the key's squares mean two things (interaction).
8. Colour is nearly all steel and green. Feedback asks for a grounded plate for the family's things, and for the plans cyan at full strength.
9. Smaller faults: drive direction glued to the minutes, Ideas filters in a boxed panel, the chat's times switching sides of the axis, month tube days that are pictures and not links, and a cramped phone bar.

The title 'Anything to plan?' was judged a yes/no question that invites 'no'. Heat a's lenses named 'What's our plan?' the standard for Pocket. Soul scored 8.5 but wants the afterglow back and amber taken off routine noise.

To win, the lineage has to keep the diary row as the app's date grammar and fix those faults without becoming a tidy copy. Trimmed (7.53) fixed every fault and still read as its parent, because a refinement must move Home's first screen. It also has to bring the original tube's light back where the phosphor is (E7 under the box, E1 on the key word, breathing lamps, a visible phosphor afterglow, the landed flash), and carry the spine with its plates and squares through Plans, To do, Settings and the form, so it reads as a system.

briefs.name: Pocket Diary, Kept
briefs.hypothesis: Pocket Diary already won on the strongest idea in the tour: a date set as a diary sets it, on one line of time. It lost points only on faults that are cheap to fix and repeat across lenses: amber spent on noise, a dead gap, a time said twice, fine print in every foot, an afterglow nobody sees, tracked plate caps, a checkbox 200px from its words, and a page that is green and grey alone. If it fixes each fault where the judges saw it, adds three visible changes to Home's first screen (a shelf hung on its own line instead of four boxes, the greeting lit from below through scanlines, the new title), and gives the light back to the plates, lamps and rows, it should keep its 8.5 type and usability and lift system, skeptic and feedback (7.2 to 8.1) to the same level. Trimmed showed that fixes alone read as the parent, which is why this brief also requires the first-screen change.
briefs.brief:
Start from t2-pocket-graft's files (palette json, sheet.css, templates, static/icons.svg). Keep the lineage at a glance: the 1px steel spine at the same x on every page, the NOW, NEXT, LATER and Someday plates, the diary row (.day: big light Plex Sans figure, Plex Mono month over weekday, then time, entry, how far off), the NEXT tube with its four-week pulse trace and shaded weekends, To do's due queue with the lit NOW line, and the Plans agenda beside the month tube.

PALETTE (t2-pocket-graft.json): glow 0.95 to 1.0 and screenGlow 1.0, and add topGlow 1.0 so E6's haze shows under the bar. brand, screen and halo stay exactly #6dff9c. Grounded colour with a job:
- Kind colours only in the 1px ring round a kind glyph, in low-chroma earth: outing moss #a9c48a, trip denim #8fb0cf, restaurant clay #cf8f72, activity wheat #c9b072, show heather #b49ac8, seasonal terracotta #d18a62. This frees amber (people #eaa85d) for late and needs-a-look only.
- The plans cyan #98dcef on .day-m at full strength, at 13px, 600 weight.

HOME, first screen (it must not read as the parent):
1. NOW. The NOW plate and today's lit '30' stay. Give the ask box E7: `.page-home .ask` gets `radial-gradient(70% 90% at 0% 100%, rgb(109 255 156 / .13), transparent 62%)` over its fill. A `::before` adds 1-in-4 white 2.8% scanlines, masked to the same corner (`mask-image: radial-gradient(60% 90% at 0% 100%, #000, transparent 75%)`), plus E4's resting halo. Set the question at 44px (34px on a phone) in Instrument Sans 600 at 84%. The lit word gets E1's full two-layer halo. It stays the largest head on Home.
2. THE SHELF. The right column (Finish setting up, To do, The kids' wishes) loses its four boxed trays. It hangs on its own short 1px steel line at the shelf's left edge, and each section plugs in at an 8px square node: amber filled for setup (needs a look), steel filled for To do, steel hollow for wishes. Each head runs its hairline out to its links, and rows are hairline-ruled with no panel fill. The line ends at a T where the shelf ends. On a phone the shelf stays where it is in reading order, on the main line.
3. Home's To do on the shelf keeps the lit NOW line between late and the rest. Its rows are tick + title + who + note, with the tick beside the title.
4. NEXT. Keep the tube and the trace. Day numbers under the pulses go to 13px (label size), with only the next pulse's number lit. The chin legend reads 'Next four weeks · weekends shaded' (already sentence case). Keep 'pointing at a plan lights its pulse' (sheet.css ~1979), and make it fire on :focus-within and on tap too.

HOME, below:
5. Coming up rows keep the diary row. Cap the row at 46rem so 'in 4 days' does not drift 300px from the entry.
6. LATER / Lately added. Cap the list at the main column's measure (about 48rem, level with Coming up's right edge). Set the row as ring | title + kind word (ink-2, 15px) | 'for Maya, Theo' directly after it in a fixed 12rem column | '#1' right-aligned at the capped edge. No gap over 3rem.
7. The line stays solid from NOW to the LATER plate on desktop and phone, and turns dotted only after LATER.

PLATES (sheet.css 236-270, `.plate`): `text-transform: none; letter-spacing: 0` so they read 'Now', 'Next', 'Later', 'Someday', 'Today' in VT323 sentence case at 1.25rem. NOW and NEXT are lit glass, and NEXT breathes (E20). Later and Someday are switched-off glass on a dashed edge.

AFTERGLOW (replace L108's stepped sage, sheet.css 1544-1566). On a row the family can open (Coming up, Plans agenda, To do, Ideas, Lately added, Settings cards, Status rows), hover or focus-within lights a 2px inset left edge in #6dff9c with `box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 var(--brand), -6px 0 14px -8px rgb(109 255 156 / .55)` at once (`transition-duration: var(--glow-in)`), then fades over `--afterglow` 1.2s. Add E10's landed flash on any :target (the 2 late link, the agenda day a month cell links to, #late, #worth).

TO DO (tasks.html):
- Row: steel node square on the spine (6px, no longer a checkbox) | .day figure (24px) | time (Plex Mono 14px) | 44px tick with its 20px well | title #id | who | how far off | Edit (pencil + word).
- The tick sits beside the title, never on the spine. The key's squares now mean only the line's states.
- The time appears once, in its column. The due words drop it: 'was due 3 days ago', 'due tomorrow'. Late words and the late row's figure are amber.
- The NOW dashed line and lit plate stay. Someday plate, then dotted.
- On a phone, stack the figure and time over the title so titles stop wrapping.
- Head: '4 open · 2 late'. '4 open' is plain text, not a link; '2 late' is the one amber link, to #late, with the landed flash.

STATUS (status.html line 58):
- The head figure reads '6 working · 7 off', plus an amber '1 needs a look' only when a part really does.
- Remove `n_worth` from the head. The odd calls go under Recent activity as a neutral ink line, '6 calls ended oddly · see them', linked to #worth, with no amber.
- Every node and lamp takes its state from the same check as its words. Any row about signing in or this page's password is amber whenever Settings' Sign-in card says it needs a look: no lamp that lies.
- Live lamps breathe (E20). Off lamps are hollow steel.
- The spend tube stays first on the line as Status's NOW stop.

SETTINGS:
- Keep the card that needs a look first, level with an amber node.
- On the section pages' side line (General shot), Sign-in's node is amber there too. This page's node is the lit square.

FOOTER KEY (base.html line 143):
- Remove `.foot-key` from base.html. Print it only on Status and Settings, as 'What the marks mean', set at 13px+ under the page head, with only the shapes that page uses.
- On a phone it is a `<details>` disclosure.
- Every other foot is the mark, the motto and the legal line.

PLANS:
- Month tube days that hold a plan become links (`<a href="#d-2026-10-04">`) to the agenda row with that id, 44px cells on a phone. Today's cell stays inverse-lit.
- Agenda rows get `id=d-YYYY-MM-DD` and the landed flash.
- Week ranges ('28 Sep – 4 Oct') are plain 14px mono label text with a short 6px tick, distinct from section nodes.
- Rename the keys to 'Coming' and 'Month' (the Month view is agenda + tube; say so in its lede).

IDEAS:
- The Drive column splits into Drive ('27 min', tabular, right-aligned) and Way ('S'), each its own column (T1-29 standard).
- Filters leave the boxed panel. They become one unboxed row plugged into the spine at a node, like To do's quick add: search field, Kind, Status, For, and one Filter key. On a phone it is a `<details>` 'Filter: any kind · anyone'.
- 'Save a thought for later' stays a fold on its node.

CHAT:
- Times leave the bubbles' sides and hang in one right-aligned tabular Plex Mono column just left of the axis. Vera's lines end 4.5rem left of the axis to clear it, and the family's start 1rem right of it.
- Only her newest stop on the axis is lit, with the arrival flash on #latest. Older marks are matte.
- The day stop is the .day figure, centred on the axis on desktop and phone.
- The NOW tab stays lit on the box.

FORM (new idea) and every settings form: the form's own short line, with a square node per field group. The node beside the focused field lights (`:focus-within`, E4 colours), and the Add key's node lights when Title and Kind are filled (`:has(:valid)`).

PHONE BAR: Memory, Family, Status and Settings stay labelled in the top bar, at 44px each, with 13px labels. Below 400px the wordmark text hides and the mark stays.

STYLE.md header in sheet.css: update the steps and the shapes' key (five shapes, one meaning each). Keep every target at 44px.

briefs.avoids:
- Thumbnail sameness: Trimmed's fate, avoided by changing Home's first screen with the unboxed shelf on its own line, the lit-from-below box and the new title.
- The false amber alarm.
- The dead gap in LATER.
- The time said twice.
- Fine print in every footer.
- The invisible afterglow.
- Tracked caps.
- A checkbox far from its words, and squares with two meanings.
- A green-and-grey-only palette.
- A lamp that lies about sign-in.

briefs.title: What’s our *plan*? It keeps the best title the lineage has found. Heat a's lenses named it the standard for Pocket in round 2 (best or joint best in six of eight notes: soul, style, system, type, usability, interaction). It replaces 'Anything to plan?', which ten notes called a yes/no question that invites 'no'. The household's 'our' fits a family diary, and 'plan' names the planner's whole job: weekends, ideas kept, the calendar, reminders, wishes. The lit word closes the line against the question mark, where the eye stops, and at 16 characters it holds one line at 44px and at 34px on a phone. It never repeats the 'Next' plate below it.

briefs.name: Diary in Ink
briefs.hypothesis:
A pocket diary is two hands on one page: the printed dates and the family's handwriting. Pocket Diary has the print and none of the hand, which is why feedback calls it 'steel, grey and amber' and asks for a grounded plate for the family's things. Three gems rebuilt in the diary's terms give it the hand:
- Kitchen Clock's two inks (L004): the family's hand is blue-black ink, the machine's is phosphor.
- Glow Ink Zine's pencilled margin notes (L164): how far off a thing is, written as a pencil note beside the printed date.
- Single Quote's setup cut to one line (L042): setup becomes a single amber stop on the spine, freeing the shelf so To do stands beside the box.

Each replaces something the page already says, which lessons say is how a graft takes, and none restates a fact in a code. Home's first screen changes (the shelf is To do, not setup, and the fields and family lines are ink). The colour becomes grounded with a job, and the diary metaphor becomes literal in a way no other lineage can claim.
briefs.brief:
Start from t2-pocket-graft's files. The idea stays recognisable at a glance: the steel spine, the Now, Next, Later and Someday plates, the diary row, the NEXT trace, To do's lit NOW line, the Plans agenda with the month tube. New here: the family's hand drawn in ink and pencil, and setup as one stop.

1. INK: the family's hand is blue-black ink, the machine's is phosphor (L004, rebuilt).
New tokens in sheet.css `:root`, low-chroma blue-black, never navy:
- `--ink-well: #0c131b` and `--ink-well-edge: #2b3d52` for a field at rest.
- `--ink-plate: #152131` and `--ink-edge: #2a3c55` for a slip.
- `--ink-cap: #7f9cbf`, a 2px cap only.

Ink goes on exactly three kinds of solid, and nowhere else. Everything else stays slate and steel; links stay denim #9db6d6 and underlined, and no text is coloured ink, so ink never reads as a link.
(a) Every field the family writes in: Home's ask textarea (inside the lit box, the well is ink while the frame stays phosphor), To do's 'What needs doing…', Ideas search, the chat composer, every form input and select, and the select's open list. Rest: ink fill and ink edge. Focus: E4's phosphor edge, ring and bloom, unchanged. So the family writes in ink and the machine lights it.
(b) The family's lines in Chat. Each is an ink slip: --ink-plate fill, 1px --ink-edge, a 2px --ink-cap along the edge nearest the axis, and the speaker's initial square on the axis in ink. Vera's lines stay dark glass with her name in sage (--lit), with a faint phosphor pool rising from the slip's foot (`inset 0 -18px 24px -20px rgb(109 255 156 / .25)`). Who spoke reads by material as well as by side.
(c) Who a thing is for: the 'Alex', 'Sam', 'Household' and 'for Maya, Theo' tags on To do, on Home's To do and LATER, and on the Ideas table. Each is a small ink tag: an --ink-plate pill with a 2px radius, a person glyph, 14px ink-2 words, 28px tall, inside a 44px row.
Not as a fill behind whole rows. Lessons say navy fills in a chat read as an editor's selection; slips are small and the cap is 2px.

2. PENCIL: how far off is a pencilled margin note (L164, rebuilt).
- The 'how far off' column of every diary row is set in Victor Mono italic 400 at 15px, graphite #aab2ae, with no tracking: 'in 4 days', 'in 2 weeks', 'tomorrow', 'yesterday' and 'was due 3 days ago'. Pages: Home Coming up, the Plans agenda and list, To do, and Home's To do.
- Late notes are amber #eaa85d with a hand underline. Rebuild r12-wild-1/static/scrawl.svg as static/scrawl.svg with an amber stroke, used as `background: url(scrawl.svg) left bottom / 100% .32em no-repeat`. The words still say 'was due', so forced-colors loses nothing.
- 'today' on the Plans agenda stays the machine's word: Plex Sans 600 in phosphor with E1, not pencil.
- Pencil is never used on a control, a fact, a figure, a head or anywhere on glass. It is the one script, with one job.
- Font: Victor Mono from the harness library, italic 400 only, subset to Latin.
- Update the sheet's header type list: four voices, one job each, plus VT323 on glass only.

3. SETUP AS ONE STOP ON THE LINE (L042, rebuilt in the spine's terms).
- 'Finish setting up' leaves the shelf. On Home's main line, directly under the ways to start and before NEXT, it is one stop: an 8px amber filled square node on the spine, an amber 1px turn-in, then one unboxed line on slate.
- The line reads: the amber figure '3' (Instrument Sans 600, 28px, tabular), 'steps before it's ready', then 'Next: Choose your own password' as the one link (bold, 17px), then a 'See all 3' `<details>` disclosure at the right that opens the three steps as a short sub-line of hollow squares.
- Amber is only in the node, the figure and the turn-in. No amber gradient and no box. 64px tall. Shown only while setup is unfinished (the same condition as today's tray).

4. HOME RESTACKED (consequence of 3).
- The shelf now opens with To do, level with the box's top. It hangs on its own short steel line, unboxed: hairline rows, the head's rule running out to '4 open · 2 late'. Under it is The kids' wishes, as ink tags with '0 open'.
- To do on the shelf keeps the lit NOW line between late and the rest, with tick + title + ink who-tag + pencil note.
- First screen at 1280: NOW plate and '30', the box with the question, the setup stop, the NEXT tube top, and To do beside them.

THE LINEAGE'S MOST IMPORTANT FIXES, also applied:
- Status: the '6 worth a look' amber head figure removed. Recent activity gets a neutral line, '6 calls ended oddly', linked to #worth. Lamps take their state from the same check as Settings, so sign-in is amber on both.
- LATER rows capped at the main column's measure, with 'for' as an ink tag right after the title and #n at the capped edge.
- To do: the time appears once, in the diary stack; the pencil note says 'due tomorrow' without it. The tick sits beside the title, and the spine node is a separate 6px steel square.
- The footer key only on Status and Settings, 13px+.
- Row afterglow as a phosphor 2px left edge, lit at once and fading over 1.2s.
- Plates in sentence case with no tracking.
- Palette glow and screenGlow 1.0, topGlow 1.0. The ask box keeps E7's glow from below with scanlines in its bottom-left corner. The question is 44px with the E1 halo.

CARRY THROUGH EVERY PAGE:
- Plans: diary rows with pencil notes, ink tags for who where a plan names people. The month tube's plan days link to their agenda rows.
- To do: ink quick-add well, ink who-tags, pencil notes, amber scrawl on late.
- Settings: every field an ink well. The Sign-in card's amber node stays.
- Chat: ink slips and glass lines, with all times in one tabular column left of the axis.
- The form: ink wells, with the field group's node lit on focus.
- Status: no ink except the 'ended oddly' line in neutral ink-2.
- Sign in: the password well is ink.
briefs.borrows:
1. L004, GEM: Two inks, phosphor for the machine's voice, blue-black for the family's hand. From r4-rand-3 Kitchen Clock (round 4, 5.56, #7 of 12).
- Source files: rounds/r4/palettes/r4-rand-3.json (field #0b121a, surface-3 #1b2633, bubble-them #1b2633, `.chip`, `.said-them .bubble`), and Sonar Watch's logbook ink in rounds/r4/palettes/r4-rand-4.json (`--log #141d27`, `--log-edge #263444`).
- Cross-check: the track lineage's current rebuild in tour/t3-a/variants/t2-track-graft/sheet.css (`--ink-plate:#182536; --ink-edge:#2e4460; --ink-well:#0d141c`), which style called 'the best grounded companion in the heat'.
- Here it replaces steel field wells, the family's slate chat bubbles and the plain 'who' words on To do, Home and Ideas. It answers feedback's 'give the family's things a grounded plate (slate-blue or ink)'.

2. L164, GEM: Relative time as a pencilled margin note. From r12-wild-1 Glow Ink Zine (round 12, 4.52, #17 of 17).
- Source files: rounds/r12/variants/r12-wild-1/sheet.css `.rel` (~1189) and the `.when .warn` scrawl rule (~1188-1195), plus static/scrawl.svg.
- Here it replaces the Plex Sans 'how far off' cell of every diary row (sheet.css 1226-1243 and To do's 2431-2443). The scout marked it as suiting Pocket ('human margin notes along the spine').
- Kept to the type judge's own fix: script for the note only, amber not red.

3. L042, GEM: Setup cut to one line. From r12-wild-4 Single Quote (round 12, 6.59, #11 of 17).
- Source files: rounds/r12/variants/r12-wild-4/sheet.css `.alert`, `.alert .legend`, `.alert-figure`, `.alert-one`, `.alert .rest` (~1119-1137), and templates/home.html.
- Here it replaces the boxed 'Finish setting up' tray on Home's shelf (home.html, sheet.css 'The shelf' ~1299-1325) with a stop on the spine. The scout marked it for Pocket ('setup as one line above the spine, so NOW keeps the top').
- Following its caveats: slate body, amber only in the node and figure, sentence-case legend.

Universal fixes taken freely: 44px targets, sentence-case plates and links, late shown in words, tabular figures, underlined links, a strong 'here'.

The lineage's fixes, as asked by its lenses:
- Status amber: seven lenses.
- LATER gap: all eight.
- Time once on To do: six.
- Footer key: style, system, skeptic.
- Phosphor afterglow: soul, system.
- Checkbox beside title: interaction.
briefs.avoids:
- 'Mostly grey, colour almost all steel' (feedback, system): ink adds a grounded blue-black with one job.
- Home's first screen reading as its parent (style), and Home being 1719px tall (interaction): setup shrinks to one 64px stop and To do moves up beside the box.
- The boxed shelf as the generic part of the page (style, round 1).
- Chat telling speakers apart by side alone.
- The rest of the lineage's faults, as in the refinement: the amber noise, the LATER gap, the double time, the footer key, the invisible afterglow, tracked plates, and the far checkbox.
- Lessons' warnings:
  - Ink is never a row fill or text colour, so there is no selection blue and no link confusion.
  - Pencil is never on a control or a fact, so it restates nothing in a code. It is the same words in a hand.
  - The setup stop has no amber gradient (Single Quote's caveat).
  - None of the main line's structures are imported: no cased terminal column, programme bands, matte plate or quote board.
briefs.title:
What should we *plan*? Not yet tried. It keeps what the judges liked across both rounds: the household's 'we', the job word 'plan' lit, and the lit word closing the line where the eye stops. It also answers the objections to its neighbours:
- It is an open question that cannot be answered 'no', unlike 'Anything to plan?'.
- It does not assume a plan already exists, the skeptic's doubt about 'What's our plan?' and 'What's the plan?'.
- It drops the 'shall' seven notes found stiff in 'What shall we plan?'.

It reads as an invitation to tell Vera a weekend, an idea to keep, a reminder or a wish, and suits a diary someone is about to write in. At 20 characters it holds one line at 44px on desktop and at 34px on a phone, and it says nothing that the Next plate below it already claims.
